patch.value: The Implementation Council workflow SHALL be defined as a deterministic staged state machine with at minimum the stages: Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze, and SHALL include an explicit checkpoint boundary at every stage transition. The orchestrator MAY refine these minimum stages into explicitly-mapped sub-stages (e.g., WorkPlanning, PatchApply, IntegrateAndValidate) provided the mapping is declared and checkpoint/stage_handoff requirements apply to both minimum stages and declared sub-stage transitions.

Stage sequence includes at minimum Intake → Generate → Validate → Review → Judge → Freeze (optionally with explicitly-mapped sub-stages), and a checkpoint boundary is recorded at every declared stage/sub-stage transition.

patch.value: Parallel lane execution with deterministic merge ordering independent of wall-clock completion timing to maximize throughput while preserving reproducibility. (See DEC1, DEC3)

Dedicated Integration sub-flow (C18→C19→C20→C21) as a first-class workflow stage with its own validation, review, and repair cycle to catch cross-lane regressions and merge conflicts. (See DEC1, DEC3)
Namespaced workspace partitions (C22) isolating per-lane canonical/non-canonical content with a shared integration partition, unified under workspace_index.json. (See DEC1)

Medium HITL strictness: automated lane-level validation with HITL triggers concentrated at integration conflicts exceeding deterministic thresholds, security critical findings, secrets detection, and ChangeRequest approvals. (See DEC4, DEC3)
Two-tier acceptance: lane-scoped gates must pass before fan-in; integrated state must pass full system-level validators, integration review, and judge assessment before freeze. (See DEC5, DEC2)
Sandboxed tooling with deny-by-default network, repo-write only via patch_apply, and per-stage tool permission matrix enforced by C11. (See DEC4)
Deterministic smallest-passing-repair selection (fewest ops → fewest bytes → first-generated) applied at both lane and integration repair stages. (See DEC1)
Stage handoff artifacts emitted at every checkpoint boundary (lane transitions, integration transitions, judge, freeze) for cold-start resumability. (See DEC2)

patch.value: Integration conflict_report (structured JSON artifact; schema/format to be specified as part of conflict-resolution policy; must include evidence pointers to conflicting patchsets/files and chosen deterministic escalation path).

How should conflict resolution work when parallel implementation pods produce overlapping/competing patchsets (merge strategy, deterministic ordering rules, reroute/rebase stages, escalation thresholds), and what is the required schema/format for the structured integration conflict_report artifact?
